messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the order in which you add numbers can affect the result due to rounding errors. For example, (a + b) + c ≠ a + (b + c) because the intermediate result of a + b may not be exactly representable as a floating-point number, leading to a different final result when adding c. This is because floating-point arithmetic is based on a finite set of representable numbers, and the intermediate results may not be exactly representable, causing the order of operations to affect the outcome.
